title: Docker & OCI Container Engineering
summary: Master Docker containerization, multi-stage distroless builds, non-root user execution, OCI layer caching, OverlayFS storage drivers, and rootless daemon security architecture.
learningObjectives: Build hardened, minimal OCI container images using multi-stage Dockerfiles and distroless base images.
Inspect and troubleshoot container filesystem layers, copy-on-write (COW) mechanics, and OverlayFS storage driver directories.
Enforce non-root execution contexts, unprivileged user namespaces, and container resource limits.

curriculumModules.title: Multi-Stage Builds, Distroless Images & Layer Optimization
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Multi-stage builds separate build-time dependencies (compilers, SDKs, dev headers) from runtime environments. Using gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot as the final stage eliminates package managers, shells, and system utilities, drastically shrinking attack surface and image size down to minimal static binaries.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Leverage Docker BuildKit cache mounts (--mount=type=cache) and multi-stage pipelines to compile Golang, Rust, or Java binaries, then copy only the stripped executable, CA certificates, and non-root /etc/passwd entries into distroless.

curriculumModules.title: Rootless Containers, User Namespaces & Security Contexts
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Running container daemons or payloads as root inside a container represents severe privilege escalation risk if container escape vulnerabilities emerge. Rootless Docker and user namespaces map container UID 0 to an unprivileged subuid on the host, preventing host root compromise.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce USER 65532:65532 (nonroot) in Dockerfiles and configure RootlessKit or user namespace remapping (userns-remap) across production worker nodes.

curriculumModules.title: OverlayFS Architecture: LowerDir, UpperDir, Merged & WorkDir
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Docker's default storage driver on Linux is overlay2. OverlayFS merges read-only image layers (lowerdir) with a single read-write container layer (upperdir) using workdir for atomic copy-on-write transactions, presenting a unified filesystem view at merged.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Avoid writing transient or ephemeral logs directly into the container's writable layer (upperdir); route telemetry to stdout/stderr or ephemeral volume mounts to prevent storage driver exhaustion.

labs.title: Hardening Microservices with Multi-Stage Distroless Builds
labs.scenario: A security scan flagged severe vulnerabilities in an enterprise payment API running as root with full bash shells and package managers. You must create a multi-stage Dockerfile, build a hardened distroless image tagged 'payment-api:distroless', launch the container with exposed port 8080, and verify its non-root security context.
labs.productionContext: Distroless images strip shells, package managers, and standard utilities, preventing attackers from downloading tools or executing interactive shells during Remote Code Execution (RCE) incidents.
objectives: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile targeting gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
Build the hardened container image tagged payment-api:distroless
Run the container in detached mode named secure-api exposing port 8080
Inspect container configuration and verify non-root user execution

steps.title: Create Multi-Stage Dockerfile
steps.instruction: Create a multi-stage `Dockerfile` with a Go builder stage and a final `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` stage.

steps.title: Build Distroless Container Image
steps.instruction: Build the container image and tag it as `payment-api:distroless`.

steps.title: Deploy Hardened Container
steps.instruction: Launch the container in detached mode named `secure-api` exposing port 8080.

steps.title: Verify Non-Root Execution Context
steps.instruction: Inspect the container's configuration using `docker inspect secure-api` to confirm user context.

validationRules.description: Built hardened image payment-api:distroless via multi-stage Dockerfile
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker build -t payment-api:distroless .' to build the image.

validationRules.description: Started secure-api container with port mapping 8080:8080
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker run -d --name secure-api -p 8080:8080 payment-api:distroless' to launch the container.

validationRules.description: Inspected container metadata and verified non-root security context
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker inspect secure-api' to audit container security context and user.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you build the image tagged payment-api:distroless, run it named secure-api, and inspect it.

labs.title: OverlayFS Storage Driver, Layer Inspection & Garbage Collection
labs.scenario: High node disk utilization was reported on a container host. You must start a caching container, inspect its OverlayFS GraphDriver paths (LowerDir, UpperDir, MergedDir), analyze filesystem modifications made in the writable layer via docker diff, and prune dangling unused image layers.
labs.productionContext: Understanding OverlayFS copy-on-write overhead and container writable layer growth is critical to preventing root partition disk exhaustion in production container hosts.
objectives: Launch redis cache container named cache-worker
Inspect container GraphDriver and OverlayFS directory paths
Inspect filesystem layer mutations using docker diff
Prune dangling image layers to reclaim host disk space

steps.title: Launch Caching Container
steps.instruction: Run a Redis container named `cache-worker` on port 6379 in detached mode.

steps.title: Inspect OverlayFS GraphDriver
steps.instruction: Inspect `cache-worker` using `docker inspect` to view LowerDir, UpperDir, and MergedDir paths.

steps.title: Track Filesystem Layer Modifications
steps.instruction: Audit container filesystem layer writes and mutations with `docker diff cache-worker`.

steps.title: Garbage Collect Dangling Images
steps.instruction: Reclaim host disk storage by pruning dangling unused image layers.

validationRules.description: Started cache-worker container with redis image
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker run -d --name cache-worker -p 6379:6379 redis:7.2-alpine' to start the cache worker.

validationRules.description: Inspected container GraphDriver and OverlayFS storage paths
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker inspect cache-worker' to inspect the OverlayFS mount points.

validationRules.description: Analyzed writable layer mutations with docker diff
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker diff cache-worker' to inspect modified files.

validationRules.description: Reclaimed disk space by pruning dangling image layers
validationRules.remediation: Run 'docker image prune -f' to remove unreferenced image layers.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you launch cache-worker, inspect it, run docker diff cache-worker, and prune images.

assessmentQuestions.question: In a production multi-stage Docker build targeting Go or Rust, why is gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot superior to alpine:latest as a runtime base?
options: (Recommended) Distroless completely omits package managers (apk) and interactive shells (/bin/sh), preventing attackers from executing secondary payload downloads during RCE.
Distroless contains a full glibc runtime with debugging utilities pre-installed.
Alpine images cannot run compiled Golang static binaries due to kernel incompatibility.
Distroless automatically compiles source code without needing a builder stage.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Distroless images include only the application binary and minimal runtime dependencies (like CA certificates, tzdata, and /etc/passwd entries for non-root users). Omitting package managers and shells drastically reduces the attack surface and renders typical web-shell or script injection attacks inert.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Linux OverlayFS (overlay2), where are newly created files and modifications written when a container is executing?
options: (Recommended) Into the read-write upperdir layer, while deleted files from lowerdir are masked with character device whiteout files.
Directly into the read-only lowerdir image layers via kernel bypass.
Into the ephemeral workdir which persists across container restarts.
Directly into the host /var/log directory via a kernel redirect loop.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: OverlayFS constructs a union mount where image layers form read-only lowerdir paths, and the container's mutable state resides in upperdir. Deletions of underlying lowerdir files are represented in upperdir as character device whiteouts (c 0 0).
